comments.author: Alexander Terp
comments.body:
Now has evidence rather than only a principle behind it. The gate was
red at HEAD and nobody knew: ./dev handed the pinned herdr down as a
repo-relative path, cargo runs an integration test from its own
package root, and so every daemon-backed test since the harness landed
(64d46d0) died at startup. Fixed in 11f7301.

That is exactly the failure a push-triggered gate catches on the commit
that causes it rather than a day later, and it is the second argument
for this card: the README's claim being true matters less than the gate
being watched.

creator: Alexander Terp
description:
The README says CI runs exactly what ./dev runs, and there is no CI - no .github/workflows at all. The claim should be true or the sentence should go.

Most of the cost is already paid: deps/herdr.pin fetches and checksums the daemon, deps/ghostty.pin builds libghostty, and ./dev with no flags is the whole gate. What a workflow adds is caching those two (libghostty is minutes cold) and choosing which platforms to run - macOS is where the shell builds, and the Linux container is where the herdr corpus gets diffed (a_26BJG8nDs).
title: 🏗️ CI: run the gate on every push
